Integrated Experimental and Machine Learning for Optimization and Performance 
Prediction of Cobalt-Based Metal-Organic Framework-Coated Nickel Foam Electrodes 
for Symmetric Supercapacitors
Radhakrishnan K1, Rohit Kumar Shaw1, D V Siva Krishna Rao K1, Aditya Kumar1,*
Department of Energy and Environment, National Institute of Technology, Tiruchirappalli, Tamil Nadu, India
*Corresponding Author: adityakumar@nitt.edu
Abstract:
Key challenges in designing high-performance metal–organic framework (MOF)-based 
supercapacitor electrodes include optimizing precursor concentration and properly predicting 
electrochemical performance. In this article, we provide an integrated experimental and 
machine learning (ML) framework to optimize Co-MOF-coated nickel foam electrodes 
manufactured via a simple and scalable dip-coating process. Concentration-dependent 
structural and morphological evolution was validated by X-ray diffraction (XRD) and scanning 
electron microscopy (SEM), with the 3 mmol Co precursor electrode (NFC3) showing the most 
uniform coating and superior electrochemical performance. The improved NFC3 electrode was 
built into an NFC3//NFC3 symmetric supercapacitor with a specific capacitance of 19.97 F 
g−1 at 1 A g−1 and 72% capacitance retention after 1000 charge–discharge cycles. 
Electrochemical studies, such as cyclic voltammetry (CV), galvanostatic charge–discharge 
(GCD), electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), Ragone analysis, b-value and Dunn's 
analysis, demonstrated that the charge storage process was mostly surface-controlled 
capacitive. Five ML regression models were trained using experimentally generated CV data 
to predict the electrochemical current response. Among these, the Random Forest model had 
the highest prediction accuracy (R² = 0.999825, RMSE = 1.28 × 10⁻⁴ A, MAE = 3.10 × 10⁻⁵ 
A). The proposed experimental-ML framework provides an effective technique for optimizing 
MOF-based electrodes and accelerates the data-driven creation of high-performance symmetric 
supercapacitors.
Keywords: Co-MOF; Nickel foam electrode; Symmetric Supercapacitor; Machine Learning; 
Random Forest Regression; Electrochemical Energy Storage; Current Response Prediction.

ABSTRACT  
Lignin-activated carbon (AC) composites were employed as electrode active materials to develop more envi -
ronmentally friendly Supercapacitor (SC) materials with enhanced properties. This way, the hydroquinone/ 
quinone moieties present in lignin molecules added Faradaic processes to the system, and the capacitance of the 
active material increased, making it appropriate for future applications requiring more efficient and sustainable 
active materials. Lignin, a sustainable biobased aromatic polymer high in carbon content, was deposited on AC 
surface employing ultrasound (US) system, and for a better deposition, AC was treated with HNO
3
. Since the 
composition and properties of lignin can vary depending on their isolation process, two different types of lignin 
were used: Kraft lignin (KL) and Organosolv lignin (OL), and the effects on the chemical and electrochemical 
composition were deduced. Physicochemical, morphological, and electrochemical analyses were carried out on 
the lignin-AC composite to determine the optimum material combination and treatment process. It was observed 
that the acid treatment was effective in enhancing the functionality and porosity of the surface. Additionally, it 
improved the deposition of lignin and facilitated the formation of hierarchically porous structures on the surface 
of treated activated carbon (TAC), with different tendencies depending on the lignin employed. The creation of 
highly porous structures also resulted in enhanced electrochemical performance in materials. This validated the 
process, where eco-innovative technologies like US forces and employment of lignocellulosic biomass compounds 
like lignin were used as sustainable and efficient alternatives for obtaining electrochemically active materials.   
1. Introduction 
Lignin-based electrode materials are gaining interest due to their 
sustainability and high availability. Most of the works of lignin incor -
poration into batteries are based on its conversion into carbon materials, 
and substitution of the currently used non-renewable fossil-based car -
bons [ 1 ]. Lignin is a promising candidate due to its high carbon content 
and unique aromatic nature. Moreover, by modulating its structure, 
different carbon materials can be obtained to meet the diverse re -
quirements of different battery types. Porous carbons derived from 
lignin have been fabricated as active materials of electrodes [ 2 ]. Lignin- 
derived carbons have also been used as active materials in SCs [ 3 ], with 
studies exploring different activation processes, including carbonization 
and combinations with polymers like polyacrylonitrile (PAN) or 
different metal oxides [ 4 ]. However, these processes are energy 
demanding. Therefore, alternative approaches to incorporate lignin into 
Energy Storage (ES) materials without the need for prior carbonization 
are gaining interest [ 1 , 5 – 7 ]. 
Numerous research works have focused on producing and studying 
composite or hybrid materials by combining lignin with other carbo -
naceous materials or conducting polymers. These efforts aim to enhance 
the properties of the resulting materials. Depending on their targeted 
application, different properties are needed. Nevertheless, one common 
characteristic of enhanced properties of carbon materials is their specific 
surface area (SSA). The porosity is a key factor for the battery perfor -
mance, as it eases the diffusion kinetics and strengthens the conductivity 
network of the conductive ions [ 8 ]. Activated carbon is a commonly 
used material for this reason, but different methodologies have been

ABSTRACT
This study highlights the synergistic integration of titanium dioxide (TiO
2
) with microwave-exfoliated reduced 
graphene oxide (ME-rGO) for advanced supercapacitor and sensing applications. The TiO
2 
content in the hybrid 
nanocomposite was systematically optimized to maximize performance for diverse applications. ME-rGO was 
synthesized through a combined microwave-assisted and modified Hummer ’ s route, enabling a highly conduc -
tive and defect-engineered nanocomposite. Additionally, the nanocomposites were characterized using various 
techniques, including X-ray diffraction (XRD), field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), Fourier- 
transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), and Raman spectroscopy. Electrochemical investigation revealed that 
the ME-rGO/TiO
2 
nanocomposite (TR-10) delivered a specific capacitance of 156 Fg
� 1
, nearly double that of 
pristine ME-rGO. This enhancement arises from the synergistic effect of the electric double-layer capacitance 
contributed by ME-rGO and the pseudocapacitive effect contributed by TiO
2
. The optimized TR-10 exhibited an 
excellent energy density of 7.8 Wh kg
� 1
, a power density 1.6 kW/kg and excellent cyclic stability with 94.2 % 
capacitance retention after 5000 charge-discharge cycles. The nanocomposite has also been used for the sensing 
of dopamine, and the LOD of 2.9 μ M was achieved. In conclusion, this research demonstrates the efficacy of 
metallic oxide ‑ carbon nanomaterial hybrids in producing high-performance, multifunctional electrodes, thereby 
opening up opportunities for the large-scale manufacturing of future energy storage and sensor devices.
1. Introduction
With the rapid advancement of next-generation electronics and 
portable energy devices, there has been a growing demand for advanced, 
multifunctional materials that can perform two key functions: energy 
storage and chemical or biosensing interfaces. In these situations, 
bifunctional electrode materials have emerged as strong contenders, 
specifically those with high electrochemical performance, coupled with 
molecular recognition and sensitivity in detection. [ 1 – 6 ] The two-way 
capability of such a feature is instrumental in system integration 
design, particularly for wearable electronics, implantable devices, and 
smart sensors, where component miniaturization is necessary without 
compromising versatility. Supercapacitors, also known as 
electrochemical capacitors, are best recognized for their high-power 
density, long cycle life, and fast charge-discharge capabilities. Their 
energy density typically lags behind that of batteries. [ 7 ] To enhance 
performance and multifunctionality, scientists have increasingly tar -
geted nanostructured materials with pseudocapacitive responses, high 
redox activity, and high surface areas for interaction with the electro -
lyte. [ 3 , 8 – 12 ] However, electrochemical sensors require materials with 
improved electrical conductivity, surface reactivity, and chemical 
selectivity. Creating a material that performs both functions efficiently is 
a synergistic combination of high conductivity, electroactive surface 
sites, and structural stability.
Reduced graphene oxide (rGO), which is a derivative of graphene, is 
among the most interesting materials in this group. Its superior

ABSTRACT
Biomass-derived carbon aerogels have attracted considerable attention for applications in CO
2 
capture and 
supercapacitors (SCs). However, these carbon aerogel materials often suffer from an insufficient number of active 
sites. In this study, a novel N, P co-doped porous carbon aerogel with a hierarchical structure was synthesized 
using cellulose biomass as the raw material, a NaOH/urea system as the solvent and activator, and urea and urea 
phosphate as heteroatom dopants. Owing to the synergistic effects of heteroatom co-doping and the hierarchical 
pore structure, the optimal sample, NPCA-600 – 0.5, exhibited a large specific surface area of 582.9 m
2
/g and a 
high pore volume of 0.187 cm
3
/g. It demonstrated a CO
2 
adsorption capacity of 2.89 mmol/g (25 
◦
C, 1 bar), 
along with high CO
2
/N
2 
selectivity and excellent recyclability, retaining 91 % efficiency after 10 cycles. As a SC 
electrode, NPCA-600 – 0.5 achieved a high specific capacitance of 238 F/g at 1 A/g, maintaining 80 % of its initial 
capacitance after 5000 cycles at 10 A/g. This work not only provides a promising adsorbent and electrode 
material for CO
2 
capture and supercapacitors, but also offers valuable insights for the design of advanced carbon- 
based materials.
1. Introduction
As the global population grows and industrialization expands, the 
demand for energy has led to the consumption of vast amounts of fossil 
fuels, resulting in significant greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions [1,2] . 
This situation has triggered a severe energy crisis and exacerbated the 
greenhouse effect. Carbon dioxide, in particular, stands out as the pri -
mary GHG (75 % of total GHG emissions) responsible for climate change 
and accelerated global warming [3,4] . In view of the above problems, 
the development of efficient CO
2 
capture technologies and energy 
storage devices emerges as a potent approach to alleviate the energy 
crisis and mitigate climate change [5,6] .
Based on the capture process principles, several CO
2 
capture 
methods, including chemical absorption [7] , membrane separation [8] , 
and gas – solid adsorption [9] , have undergone extensive research and 
application. Of these, gas – solid adsorption technology has emerged as a 
compelling option, thanks to its high absorption rate, convenient 
regeneration system, energy efficiency, and environmental friendliness 
[10] . Porous carbons are highly regarded as promising CO
2 
gas – solid 
adsorption materials. Their high chemical and thermal stability, exten -
sive specific surface area, adjustable pore structure make them a top 
choice [11] . Furthermore, carbon materials usually possess a layered 
porous structure alongside a substantial specific surface area. Micro -
pores and small mesopores can enhance the storage of charge ions. 
While meso-macro pores provide mass transfer channels to facilitate the 
transport of charge ions in solution [12,13] . This configuration facili -
tates the efficient transfer of ions and electrons, as well as the accu -
mulation of charge, thereby rendering them an excellent candidate for 
energy storage materials [14 – 16] .
In recent years, carbon aerogel-type porous carbon, with its three- 
dimensional structure, high surface area, high electrical conductivity 
and stable physicochemical properties, has been identified as an 
emerging class of functional materials for CO
2 
capture and super -
capacitors [17 – 19] . Zhai et al. [20] prepared the starch-based carbon 
aerogel. When used as an electrode material for supercapacitors, it 
showed excellent electrochemical properties, reaching a specific 
capacitance of 211.5 F/g at 0.5 A/g. Ji et al. [21] prepared a biochar- 
silicon hybrid aerogel using carbon nanotubes and silicon as raw ma -
terials. The hybrid aerogel exhibited good CO
2 
adsorption performance, 
with a CO
2 
adsorption capacity of 2.74 mmol/g at 25 
◦
C and 1 bar.

ABSTRACT
Onions, scientifically known as Allium cepa L., are commonly used as a vegetable and offer a variety of health 
benefits. However, this study explored a novel part of the onion plant, such as the flower seed cover often 
regarded as waste, by converting it into biochar (BC) via pyrolysis. Through careful optimization and activation 
with potassium hydroxide, the resulting novel biochar exhibited a unique graphitic nanosheet-like structure with 
an impressive surface area of 2538.31 m
2
/g. To serve as a control, rice straw, one of the most commonly used 
biomasses, was also activated using the same protocol. Various techniques, including XPS, HRTEM, SAED, FTIR, 
BET, XRD, and Raman, were used to comprehensively understand the surface and structural properties of the 
biochar. When the novel biochar was tested as an energy storage material, it exhibited a specific capacitance of 
200.37 F/g at 1 A/g and 143.82 F/g at 5 A/g in a 1 M H
2
SO
4 
electrolyte with a three-electrode system. In a two- 
electrode system, it showed 158 F/g at 1 A/g and 102 F/g at 5 A/g, indicating its effectiveness at high rates. The 
long-term cyclic stability analysis demonstrated 100 % capacity retention over 1000 cycles in the three-electrode 
system, and 90.77 % and 74.40 % retention after 5000 cycles and 10,000 cycles, respectively, in the two- 
electrode system. The fabricated symmetric supercapacitor yielded a power density of 500 W/kg and an en -
ergy density of 21.94 Wh/kg at a current density of 1 A/g. These findings provide valuable insights into the 
valorization of biomass in addressing concerns regarding the current energy storage dilemma.
1. Introduction
It is reported that the natural world produces about 50 billion tons of 
land-based biomass each year. Out of this, about 16.7 billion tons are 
used for human purposes, such as feed for livestock, food, grazing, and 
specialized crops for other purposes. What is left off after the con -
sumption of these 16.7 billion tons is about 8.1 billion tons, which can be 
sustainably harvested and recycled into value-added products [ 1 ]. 
However, due to logistical and operational challenges, many of these 
biomasses are left untouched, eventually becoming a menace to the 
environment [ 2 ]. Owing to the high cost of commercially activated 
carbon and the vast tonnages of agricultural biomasses that pile up in the 
environment, scientists have resorted to the valorization of this agri -
cultural biomass waste into biochar to be more economical and sus -
tainable due to the abundance of biomass in the environment [ 3 ].
Biochar is a beneficial substance notably rich in carbon and lignin, 
produced under oxygen-deprived conditions via the thermochemical 
conversion of biomass [ 4 ]. Many plant-based agricultural residues are 
regarded as waste, and human approaches to dealing with this waste 
tend to pollute the environment. A practical and environmentally sus -
tainable way of managing these tons of agricultural waste is by pyro -
lyzing the waste in an anoxic environment to produce biochar [ 5 ]. The 
properties of biochar, such as its large surface area, surface functional 
groups, high porosity, and stability, make it a viable alternative for

1. Introduction
The escalating global energy crisis, resulting from excessive fossil 
fuel consumption and accompanying CO
2 
emissions, has intensified the 
demand for sustainable energy solutions and advanced energy storage 
technologies [1] . Among emerging energy storage systems, super -
capacitors (SCs, also known as electrochemical capacitors) have 
garnered significant scientific attention as hybrid devices bridging the 
performance gap between conventional dielectric capacitors and 
rechargeable batteries [2,3] . These devices feature three distinct ad -
vantages over conventional energy storage systems: exceptional char -
ge/discharge kinetics that enable rapid energy delivery within seconds, 
unparalleled cycle stability exceeding 100,000 cycles with minimal 
capacitance decay, and superior power density (typically 10 – 100 times 
higher than lithium-ion batteries) [4,5] . Particularly, electrical 
double-layer capacitors (EDLCs), which rely on physical charge 
adsorption/desorption at electrode-electrolyte interfaces, demonstrate 
remarkable rate capability and cycling performance compared to pseu -
docapacitive systems [2,6] .
Carbon-based materials, including activated carbon, carbon nano -
tubes, graphene, and carbon fibers, are predominantly employed in the 
design of supercapacitor electrodes due to their tunable physicochem -
ical properties and robust electrochemical stability [7,8] . The perfor -
mance of these materials is principally governed by three critical 
parameters: (i) heteroatom doping configurations, (ii) accessible specific 
surface area (S
BET
), and (iii) hierarchical pore architecture [9,10 ] .

ABSTRACT
Carbon materials have the advantages of large surface area, high conductivity and stable chemical properties, 
and are widely used in the field of electrochemical energy storage. However, carbon materials currently have 
some problems such as high cost, complicated process and poor electrochemical performance. The development 
of low cost, environmental friendly and high specific capacitance porous carbon materials is of great significance 
for large-scale production and application. In addition, renewable, low-cost biomass materials are ideal pre -
cursors for the preparation of porous carbon materials. In this work, porous carbon materials were synthesized 
using ginkgo leaves as carbon source and KHCO
3 
as activator. The effect of activator mass on the structure and 
composition of porous carbon was studied in detail. The results show that when 3 g activator is added, the 
prepared carbon material (GCK-3) has a specific surface area of up to 2640 m
2 
g

and a rich hierarchical pore 
structure (including micro, medium and large pores). In addition, the carbon material retains a certain amount of 
the heteroatoms of the biomass itself, which can generate additional pseudocapacitance. Due to the advantages 
of composition and structure, GCK-3 shows good electrochemical performance and rate performance. A sym -
metric supercapacitor assembled from two identical GCK-3 electrodes has an energy density of 13.7 Wh kg
� 1 
and 
exhibits good cycle stability with a capacitor retention rate of 100 % after 10,000 cycles. The green and low-cost

ginkgo leaf derived carbon materials have great application prospects.
1. Introduction
With the increasingly prominent resource and environmental prob -
lems, the development and demand of electronic equipment and new 
energy vehicles are increasing rapidly, and the development of low-cost 
and high-performance energy storage equipment has become particu -
larly important [ 1 , 2 ]. Supercapacitors have the characteristics of high 
power density, high coulomb efficiency and long cycle life, which are 
the energy storage devices concerned by many researchers [ 3 – 5 ]. 
Electrode materials play an important role in the electrochemical per -
formance of supercapacitors, and also involve the manufacturing cost of 
supercapacitors [ 6 ]. Therefore, the development of low-cost and 
high-performance electrode materials has become one of the main 
research goals of supercapacitors as energy storage devices.
Porous carbon materials have high surface area, high porosity, 
excellent electrical conductivity and chemical stability, and can be used 
as high-performance electrode materials for supercapacitors. At present, 
porous carbon materials mainly composed of micropores and small 
mesoporous are widely used as electrode materials [ 7 , 8 ]. However, 
porous carbon materials often have poor pore structure and closed 
pores, which is not conducive to the improvement of electrochemical

fiber for high performance supercapacitors

ABSTRACT
By virtue of its abundant availability, diverse structures, renewability, and cheapness, the rational utilization of 
biomass waste to synthesis porous carbon with a great specific surface area (SSA), high porosity, and superior 
electrochemical capabilities holds substantial significance for energy storage. In this research, waste bamboo 
fibers with a vascular bundle structure were selected as precursors. The porosity and conductive characteristics of 
the materials (ACK-x, x represents the activation temperature) were controllably adjusted by altering the KOH 
activation temperature. The findings suggest that the material ’ s notable expansion in SSA is linked to the rise in 
activation temperature. Notably, ACK-700 has a SSA of up to 2768 m
2 
g
� 1 
and micropores comprising 80.34 % of 
the structure, which demonstrated outstanding capacitive properties of 492 F g
� 1 
at 0.5 A g
� 1
, along with low 
resistance values (the resistance value for charge transfer as low as 0.81 Ω ) in the three-electrode system. ACK- 
700 demonstrated a capacitive performance of up to 283 F g
� 1 
when assembled into a symmetrical device, 
achieving a high density of energy of 9.82 Wh ⋅ kg
� 1 
while possessing an excellent power density of 123.15 W 
kg
� 1
. The capacitance preservation was 89.44 %, and the Coulomb efficiency reached 100 % after 2000 charge- 
discharge cycles. Most importantly, we successfully demonstrated the practical viability of these materials by 
powering a 2.2 V LED bulb for 20 min using three such symmetrical supercapacitors connected in series. This 
study outlines a cost-effective and straightforward approach for preparing bamboo fiber-based porous carbon 
and highlights the significant potential of waste biomass-derived carbons for practical supercapacitor 
applications.
Waste bamboo fiber-based porous carbon was prepared from waste 
bamboo fiber as a carbon source after low-temperature carbonization 
with KOH as an activator. Then, the bamboo fiber-based porous carbon 
was characterized and assembled into a symmetric supercapacitor, 
which electrochemical performance was tested and the energy storage 
mechanism was analyzed.
1. Introduction
In view of the irreversible and progressive reduction of fossil fuels, 
developing renewable energy sources have emerged as effective strate -
gies to address the crisis of environmental damage and global warming. 
However, the key issue for the development of renewable energy is the 
availability of high efficiency, affordable and sustainable energy storage 
facilities [ 1 – 3 ]. Supercapacitors (SCs) stand out among other novel en -
ergy storage technologies owing to their affordability, fast responsive -
ness, superior power density, and simple operating environment [ 4 – 6 ]. 
SCs are prevalent utilized in sensors, industrial automation equipment ’ s 
auxiliary power supply, power grid energy storage devices, and new 
energy vehicle power systems [ 7 , 8 ]. On the basis of their energy storage 
techniques, SCs are grouped into pseudocapacitors using redox reactions 
and electrical double-layer capacitors (EDLCs) utilizing physical 
adsorption. Conductive polymers or metal oxides, which typically have 
inadequate cycling stability, are exemplary pseudocapacitors electrodes. 
Despite the fact that these materials increase the device ’ s energy den -
sity, chemical reactions cause the electrode material ’ s structure to 
deteriorate over time, leading to diminished cycling stability [ 9 ]. In 
contrast to pseudocapacitors, EDLCs employ excellently conductive 
carbon materials as electrodes. Among them, the most popular electrode 
material for EDLCs is porous carbon because of its rich pore structure, 
high conductivity, and extensive active specific surface area (SSA). 
These characteristics typically confer excellent capacitive performance 
and robust cycling stability [ 10 ].

ABSTRACT
With the development of computer technology, a variety of machine learning models have been used to predict
the electrochemical performance of energy storage devices. In this study, the elemental analysis, industrial
analysis and structural composition, activation conditions, and current density of biomass are innovatively
selected as input conditions from the biomass raw material characteristics perspective and predict specific
capacitance based on the light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM) and deep neural network (DNN) algo-
rithm. Meanwhile, the prediction effects of the contrast capacitance under seven different input combinations are
compared. The results show that the combination prediction effect of retaining all features is the best, and the
industrial analysis and structural composition of biomass have a greater impact on the model than elemental
analysis, this conclusion is also verified by SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) value analysis, indicating that
they are essential for the model. It is also found that the Light GBM model has more advantages, with R
2
of 0.951,
mean absolute error (MAE) of 11.090, and Root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 14.756. This study builds a key
bridge between the basic composition information of biomass raw materials and the electrochemical perfor-
mance. Also, it helps to understand the related formation mechanism of biomass-derived carbon materials.
1. Introduction
With the increasing emphasis on renewable energy and the
increasing demand for addressing climate change, the demand for effi-
cient energy storage technologies is becoming more and more urgent.
Therefore, creating innovative and effective energy storage solutions has
emerged as a significant global challenge [ 1 ]. Among the spectrum of
energy storage devices, supercapacitors, as a new form of energy stor-
age, have become highly promising candidates. Their advantages lie in
their high power density, wide temperature range, and economical and
environmentally friendly characteristics [ 2 , 3 ]. The selection and per-
formance of electrode materials have a crucial impact on the overall
performance and cost of supercapacitors. As a key component of the
supercapacitor structure, it directly determines its key parameters such
as electrochemical performance, energy density, power density, and
cycle life [ 4 ]. Among many electrode materials, biomass-derived carbon
has been widely used in supercapacitors due to its high specific surface
area (SSA), low cost, high porosity, large-scale production, and
environmental friendliness [ 5 , 6 ].
Although supercapacitors have been particularly widely used, man-
ufacturers are still seeking higher energy-density supercapacitors to
meet the needs of transportation, energy, and aerospace. [ 7 ] The com-
plex composition and structure of biomass make the synthesized carbon
materials often exhibit inhomogeneity [ 8 , 9 ]. Moreover, biomass-
derived carbon materials have irregular pore structures and single-
pore channels, resulting in an increase in the diffusion distance and
resistance of ions in the electrolyte, which significantly reduces the rate
performance of assembling supercapacitors [ 10 ]. Therefore, various
methods have been tried to prepare high-performance porous carbon
materials, such as the molten salt method, activation method, hydro-
thermal carbonization method, and template method [ 11 – 12 ]. In many
experiments preparing porous carbon materials for supercapacitors, a
common method is to chemically or physically activate biochar [ 11 , 12 ].
Physical activation involves subjecting carbon materials to high-
temperature atmospheres (CO2, O2, etc.) to form pores [ 13 ]. Chemi-
cal activation, on the other hand, involves using acids or strong bases

ABSTRACT
To address the optimization issue of experimental parameters during the experimental preparation of biomass 
char supercapacitors, this study applied six different regression models (four machine learning models and two 
deep learning models) to predict the specific capacitance of biomass char supercapacitors. The results indicate 
that the Transformer model performs best in terms of prediction accuracy, with an R
2 
(coefficient of determi -
nation) of 0.9609, an MAE (mean absolute error) of 16.8599, and an RMSE (root mean square error) of 19.4569. 
Furthermore, analysis indicates that among the experimental parameters, the activation temperature exerts the 
most significant influence on the specific capacitance. The carbonization temperature and carbonization time 
exhibit a strong coupled relationship with the specific capacitance: at low carbonization temperatures, 
carbonization time shows a positive correlation with specific capacitance, whereas at high carbonization tem -
peratures, carbonization time correlates negatively with specific capacitance. A high heating rate demonstrates a 
strong negative correlation with specific capacitance. This study employs regression models to analyze experi -
mental parameter data, thereby providing novel approaches for optimizing experiments aimed at designing 
superior supercapacitors.
1. Introduction
As developed and developing nations progressively implement their 
strategic objectives of carbon peaking and carbon neutrality, countries 
are gradually reducing their reliance on fossil fuel energy sources, 
decreasing the share of thermal power capacity, and pursuing greener, 
lower-carbon methods of electricity generation [ 1 ], which has fostered 
the continuous advancement of renewable energy, with particular 
emphasis on enhancing the utilization of wind and solar power [ 2 ]. 
However, unlike thermal and nuclear power these renewable energy 
sources lack the stable power output and easy-to-implement power 
regulation capabilities of generation methods. Their electricity output is 
thus subject to fluctuations due to temporal and spatial factors [ 3 ]. 
Consequently, the integration of green yet intermittent power genera -
tion methods such as wind and solar energy into the grid gives rise to a 
series of new grid challenges, including voltage fluctuations, frequency 
instability, and diminished grid frequency regulation and peak load 
management capabilities [ 4 ]. The construction of energy storage power 
plants (such as supercapacitor energy storage, electrochemical energy 
storage, pumped hydro storage, thermal energy storage, and.) is one of 
the most effective methods for addressing these issues [ 5 ].Among these, 
supercapacitor energy storage stands out as the most promising and 
sought-after energy storage device for grid frequency regulation due to 
its high power density, rapid charge-discharge capabilities, and 
extended cycle life [ 6 ]. The preparation of supercapacitors typically 
employs char-based materials. Biomass char, as a low-carbon-footprint, 
environmentally friendly, and cost-effective carbon-rich material, ex -
hibits favorable capacitive physicochemical properties, together with 
the potential of abundant functional groups, and a tunable pore struc -
ture. Consequently, it has been extensively explored for the fabrication 
of high performance supercapacitors [ 7 ].
However, biomass char derived from simple carbonization processes 
often suffers from underdeveloped pore structures, limited functional 
groups, and suboptimal surface morphologies. As a result, super -
capacitors fabricated using such char materials show suboptimal energy 
storage performance, which hinders their practical application in grid

ABSTRACT
Global transition toward sustainable and efficient energy storage has intensified research into supercapacitors, 
valued for their rapid charge-discharge capability, high power density, and long operational lifespan. Among 
carbonaceous materials, biomass-derived biochar has emerged as a low-cost, renewable, and structurally tunable 
precursor for electrode design. This review provides a structured and critical synthesis of biochar-based super -
capacitor strategies, systematically categorizing heteroatom doping, nanocomposite engineering, and hybrid 
architecture within an integrated electrochemical performance framework. Unlike existing literature that pre -
dominantly summarizes modification approaches, this review emphasizes cross-study comparability, mechanistic 
attribution, and device-level relevance to clarify transferable design principles. A consolidated analysis of recent 
machine learning (ML) applications reveals a paradigm shift from empirical optimization to data-driven pre -
dictive design. Benchmarking against reported datasets, descriptors, and model architectures, we confirm that 
tree-based ensemble and neural-network models (e.g., XGBoost, LightGBM, ANN) consistently achieve high 
predictive accuracy (R² > 0.9), while also identifying current limitations in data standardization and descriptor 
harmonization. The review critically evaluates how ML can move beyond correlation towards interpretable and 
transferable optimization under realistic device constraints.
Finally, a converging research roadmap is proposed, prioritizing standardized reporting, device-level bench -
marking, and constraint-aware ML integration to accelerate scalable implementation. By integrating materials 
engineering, data-driven modeling, and practical deployment considerations, this review establishes a compre -
hensive framework for advancing sustainable biochar-based supercapacitors toward real-world energy storage 
applications.

meeting the escalating energy requirements resulting from worldwide 
population growth [1] . Continuous development and exploration of

fuel-based energy systems. Among novel solutions, supercapacitors have 
gained remarkable prominence due to their superior power density, 
safety, cycling stability, and reversibility [2,3] . Owing to their rapid 
charging capability and excellent power performance, supercapacitors 
are increasingly used in portable electronics and electric transportation

ABSTRACT
By offering a green and sustainable option to reusing biomass, the creation of energy harvesting/storage sys-
tems from biomass/waste materials has signi ﬁcant scienti ﬁc and technological implications. To achieve the
required applications in the ﬁelds of supercapacitor and conversion, microstructure management is crucial
for carbon-based materials. Here, a facile production of heteroatom-doped porous carbon (HAPC) from
Enhydra ﬂuctuant leaves as electrode material for supercapacitor is demonstrated. Large speci ﬁc-surface area
and good pore-size distribution were achieved. An exceptional speci ﬁc-capacitance ( C
sp) 428 F/g at 1 A/g in
an acidic electrolyte was achieved. The solid-state symmetric-supercapacitor device (SSSD) produces the high-
est C
sp of 113 F/g and 73.88 Wh/kg energy –density at 1 A/g, whereas 5.11 kW/kg power-density was achieved
at 10 A/g. The SSSD exhibits outstanding durability, where it holds 94% of its Csp after 10,000 charge/dis-
charge series.
1. Introduction
A global goal is now to produce and store energy ef ﬁciently, eco-
friendly, and sustainably. Numerous rechargeable devices have been
created, and electrochemical-related technology has garnered a lot of
attention as an ef ﬁcient method for electrical energy storage. Because
of their large power capacity, outstanding coulombic reversibility
(98% or more), exceptional cyclability, and environmentally benign
characteristics, supercapacitors play a signi ﬁcant role in energy har-
vesting/storage. The pseudocapacitors and double-layer capacitors
are the two primary groups of supercapacitors based on the charge-
storage mechanism [1–4]. So, in the recent decade, the main chal-
lenges are to explore biocompatible sources which are renewable,
eco-friendly, cost-effective, and high-adsorption electrode materials,
having fast ion and/or electrode transport, and also ﬁlled with tunable
microstructure/surface chemistry [5]. Biomass is a renewable, crucial
precursor to produce carbonaceous materials for energy harvesting/
storage device applications. Therefore, nowadays researchers put more
attention into processing biomass-derived materials for their attract-
able storage properties including their extensive accessibility, being
renewable, and also cost-effective starting ingredients. As a result, var-
ious types of applications are exploited for these kinds of properties
including carbon-dioxide capture [6], hydrogen storage [7], dye-sensi-
tized solar cells [8], water treatment [9], and most importantly energy
storage [10,11]. More importantly, these are useful for their attract-
able integral homogeneous, also speci ﬁc biological properties that
are applied as patterns for constructing active electrode materials con-
necting well-deﬁned geometries. Besides this, products containing car-
bon precursor as a major quantity and also the well-balanced networks
are signi ﬁcant for the metabolic process of making biowaste-based
electrode materials. Because of this, they are appropriate for applica-
tions involving electrochemical charge/discharge that require rapid
ion movement. Recently, diverse types of biomass or biowaste-derived
carbon materials are indispensable in the fabrication of self-doped
hierarchical porous carbon-based electrodes and this gets increasing
interest as a warming theme for energy harvesting/storage and conver-
sion-related ﬁelds [12].

Biomass-derived activated carbon from Cyperus pangorei for high-performance 
supercapacitor electrodes  
N. Maheswari1* & S. Nandhini2 
1Shree Ramchandra College of Engineering, Lonikand, Pune-412216, Maharashtra, India 
2Department of Physics, M. V. Muthiah Government Arts College for Women, Dindigul-624001, Tamil Nadu, India 
*E-mail: nmahi.phys@gmail.com 
Received 30 June 2026; accepted 15 July 2026 
Activated carbon was successfully prepared from Cyperus pangorei  through a simple and cost-effective thermal 
decomposition method using ghee as a ca rbonization aid. The obtained carbon was annealed at 500 °C for 3 h and 
characterized by scanning electron microscopy  and Fourier transform infrared spec troscopy (FTIR). SEM analysis revealed 
aggregated carbon particles, while FTIR confirmed the pr esence of oxygen-containing surface functional groups. The 
electrochemical performance of the prep ared carbon electrode was evaluated usi ng cyclic voltammetry, galvanostatic 
charge-discharge, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy and cycling stability studies using PVA / Na 2SO4 gel electrolyte 
within a potential window of 0–1.5 V. The electrode  exhibited a maximum specific capacitance of 476 F g -1 and maintained 
excellent capacitive behaviour even at a high current density of 25 A g -1. The enhanced electrochemical performance is 
attributed to the combined contribution of electric double- layer capacitance and surface redox activity associated with 
oxygen-containing functional groups. The results demonstrate that Cyperus pangorei-derived carbon is a promising low-cost 
and sustainable electrode material for supercapacitor applications. 
Keywords: Activated carbon, Biomass carbon, Cyperus pangorei, Energy storage, Electrochemical performance, Supercapacitor  
Introduction 
The growing demand for sustainable energy storage 
systems has stimulated extensive research on advanced 
electrochemical energy storage devices. Supercapacitors, 
batteries, and conventional capacitors are widely used in 
energy storage technologies based on electrochemical 
energy conversion processes 1-3. Among them, 
supercapacitors have attracted significant attention 
owing to their high power density, rapid charge-
discharge capability, long cycle life, operational safety, 
and environmental friendliness 4. These characteristics 
make them suitable for applications in consumer 
electronics, backup power systems, electric vehicles and 
renewable energy storage. 
The performance of supercapacitors is strongly 
influenced by the nature of  the electrode material. 
Various electrode materials, including activated 
carbons, carbon aerogels, carbon nanotubes, graphene-
based materials, conducti ng polymers and transition 
metal oxides, have been investigated for supercapacitor 
applications. Recently, bi omass-derived activated 
carbons have attracted c onsiderable attention as 
sustainable electrode materials for high-performance 
supercapacitors owing to their low cost, renewability, 
tunable pore structure and e nvironmental friendliness. 
Recent reviews have highlighted the significant 
progress achieved in the synthesis, activation strategies, 
and electrochemical performance of biomass-derived 
carbon materials for energy storage applications
5-6.. 
Activated carbons are among the most widely used 
electrode materials because of their high specific 
surface area, excellent electrical conductivity, chemical 
stability and low cost
7. Activated carbons can be 
produced from a variety of carbon-rich precursors, 
particularly biomass wastes, which offer the advantages 
of abundance, renewability, and environmental 
sustainability
8. Numerous biomass sources such as 
palm-tree cobs, plum kernels, cassava peel, sugarcane 
bagasse, rice husks, olive stones, date pits, fruit stones 
and nutshells have been successfully utilized for the 
preparation of activated carbons
9. 
Cyperus pangorei commonly known as korai grass, 
is an abundant lignocellulosic biomass containing 
holocellulose, cellulose, hemicellulose, lignin, waxes, 
and moisture
10. Owing to its high carbon content and 
widespread availability, it represents a promising 
precursor for the preparati on of activated carbon. It 
contains cellulose, hemicellulose and lignin, which are 
known to produce a high carbon yield upon thermal 
decomposition. In addition, the fibrous structure of

1. Introduction 
Supercapacitors with super high power density, speedy charge- 
discharge rate, and exceptional operation life have emerged widely 
concerned in recent years [1 – 5] . According to the energy storage 
mechanisms, supercapacitors can be classified into pseudocapacitors 
and electric double layer capacitors. Compared with pseudocapacitors, 
electric double-layer capacitors exhibit higher cycle life and better rate 
performance. Activated carbon is the preferred electrode material for 
the commercialization of supercapacitors because of its big specific 
surface area, cheap cost, and good electrochemical stabilization [6 – 9] . 
Nevertheless, activated carbon is usually mainly composed of micro -
pores, which faces long ion migration distance, high ion migration 
resistance, and poor conductivity [10 – 12] . As a result, the electro -
chemical performance of activated carbon is not satisfactory. 
Two-dimensional (2D) porous carbon sheets have attracted massive 
attention as electrode material for supercapacitors due to their great 
open smooth layer with big specific surface area, low ion migration 
distance, and short ion migration resistance [13 – 16] . Template syn -
thesis is an available method to produce 2D porous carbon sheets. For 
example, Wei et al. [17] prepared multi-mesoporous carbon nanosheets 
using Mg(OH)
2 
as the template and hydroxyquinoline-zinc complex as 
the carbon source. The synthesized carbon nanosheets exhibit a specific 
capacitance of 220 F g

. Although some results have been 
obtained, the template method requires synthesis and removal of tem -
plates, and the preparation process is tedious, time-consuming, and 
resource-consuming. 
Recently, the preparation of two-dimensional porous carbon sheets

technology, cheap cost, and good electrochemical performance [18 – 21] .

Biomass Porous Carbon Derived from Celery Leaves with
High Capacitance for Supercapacitor
Jiaqi Wu, Zihan Ma, Guangning Wang,* and Tingting Chen*
[a]
To develop environmentally friendly and high-performance
supercapacitors, the low-cost, high-capacitance renewable
electrode material is at present viewed as one of the most
challenging tasks for obtaining the next-generation of energy
storage devices. Therefore, in this study, Celery leaves, a
common biomass vegetable, are used to prepare activated
carbon for high voltage and high-capacity supercapacitors
through a simple method. Due to their high surface area and
abundant nitrogen and sulfur heteroatoms, hierarchically
porous carbon materials can simultaneously realize high
capacity and long-cycling durability. The specific capacitance
has been recorded to be up to 753.0 F g
� 1
at 0.5 A g
� 1
with
capacity retention as high as 96.7 % even after 5,000 cycles.
Also, the assembled symmetric cell provided a high energy
density of 17.36 Wh kg
� 1
at 250 W kg
� 1
. The effects of yellow
and green colors and different activation temperatures on the
properties of electrode materials were systematically studied.
The results showed an excellent electrochemical performance
in biomass carbon electrode materials, which would facilitate
the development of a high-quality energy system and a green
supercapacitor.
Introduction
With the worsening of the environment and depletion of
resources, the human society is in crisis. Therefore, there is a
critical need to develop high energy conversion efficiency
storage devices. Supercapacitors (SCs) have attracted attention
because of the merits of large power density, good cycling
stability, fast charging, and discharging.
[1]
Thus, the super-
capacitor is being used in various ways for electronics as well
as electric vehicles with hybrid drive and pulse technology.
[2]
However, the SCs have low energy density, which limits the
range of the original application. Generally, it is proportional to
the supercapacitor’s energy density with capacitance and
voltage window.
[3]
The potential window can be increased by
assembling an asymmetric supercapacitor. Although high
capacitance electrode materials have been widely used in the
positive electrode of the asymmetric supercapacitor, it is
difficult to obtain negative electrodes that have high capaci-
tance. Generally, carbon materials with large negative potential
windows are used as negative electrode.
[4]
Carbon materials,
such as, graphene, carbon nanotubes, porous carbon, etc. are
versatile. They are not only non-toxic, chemically stable, and
readily conduct electricity, but also have peculiar properties
can accelerate electrolyte ions diffusion.
[5]
However, the low
capacitance of traditional carbon materials reduces the energy
density of SCs. Finding a negative electrode with high
capacitance remains a challenge, which limits the development
of SCs. Specifically, increasing the specific surface areas (SSA)
can improve the capacitance and rate performance by adjust-
ing the pore distribution of carbon.
[6]
The wettability can be
increased by doping heteroatoms on the carbon surface, and
the electrolyte-accessible areas can be enlarged.
[7]
However,
these electrode materials are usually prepared using expensive
and unsustainable raw materials.
[8]
Given all these require-
ments, biomass is seen as a high-efficiency carbon precursor
because of its economical and continuable potential. Using
special processes, well-distributed pore size and physicochem-
ical stability were exhibited in some biomass-derived carbons.
[9]
They have the advantages of large potential windows, stable
physicochemical properties, easy synthesis, and are often used
as a positive pole in asymmetric SCs.
[10]
Additionally, biochar
raw materials tend to contain a mass of oxygen-containing
functional groups, such as C � O, C = O, and carboxyl groups,
improving their performance over traditional carbon
materials.
[11]
For example, Wu et al. used albizia flowers to
prepare hierarchical porous carbon microrods for SCs. The
specific capacitance (Cs) reached 406 F g
� 1
at a current density
of 0.5 A g
� 1
in a 6 M KOH electrolyte.
[12]
It could improve
capacitance performance and energy storage in SCs by
selecting suitable biomass precursors and catalysts. Regarding
SCs, biomass is a promising electrode material. However, there
are still many factors preventing its further use: finiteness of
geographical distribution, production, and transportation.

good charge storage capacity, but unfortunately it was

Abstract: Supercapacitors are one of the promising devices for the accumulation and storage of
electrical energy. The purpose of this study is to develop a synthesis and modiﬁcation method of
carbon material to improve the electrochemical characteristics of a supercapacitor. In the proposed
study, by varying the sequence and parameters of the processes of carbonization, mechanoactivation
and thermochemical activation, the conditions for obtaining nanoporous carbon with a speciﬁc
surface area of 2200 (±50) m2/g from walnut shells (WSs) are optimized. In addition, to increase the
electrochemical efﬁciency of the electrode material, the resulting nanoporous carbon was modiﬁed
with nickel oxide (NiO) nanoparticles by the thermochemical method. It is shown that the modiﬁ-
cation with nickel oxide nanoparticles makes it possible to increase the speciﬁc capacitance of the
supercapacitor electrode by 16% compared to the original unmodiﬁed nanoporous carbon material.
Keywords: biomass-derived; walnut shell; activated carbon; modiﬁcation; CVD; supercapacitors
1. Introduction
Batteries (galvanic cells), capacitors, and supercapacitors are currently used as elec-
trical systems for the accumulation and storage of electrical energy. Supercapacitors, in
their electrochemical characteristics, occupy an intermediate position between batteries
and capacitors, but at the same time, they have a high speciﬁc power, a record charge and
discharge rate, and an almost unlimited service life [ 1]. Due to these advantages, they
are currently the most promising devices for the accumulation and storage of electrical
energy [2]. The paper by ¸ Sahin M et al. [3] provides a comprehensive review of the literature
on supercapacitor designs, operating principles, speciﬁcations, and classiﬁcations in a com-
parable manner, as well as a feasibility study on the use of supercapacitors in applications
such as transportation, electric vehicles, hybrid power systems, and military applications.
In recent decades, porous carbon materials obtained from biomass have become
widely used as electrode materials for supercapacitors due to their low cost, renewability,
rich reserves, environmental friendliness, and unique properties (such as large surface
area) [4]. Biomass as a feedstock for obtaining porous carbon materials is also attractive
because the problems associated with the disposal and use of plant raw materials waste
remain relevant due to environmental and economic factors [ 5,6]. The application of
biomass carbon electrode materials for the development of various types of supercapacitors

ABSTRACT
Biomass‐derived carbons are eco‐friendly and sustainable materials, making them ideal for supercapacitors due to their high
surface area, excellent conductivity, cost‐effectiveness, and environmental benefits. This review provides valuable insights into
biomass‐derived carbon and modified carbon for supercapacitors, integrating both experimental results and theoretical cal-
culations. This review begins by discussing the origins of biomass‐derived carbon in supercapacitors, including plant‐based,
food waste‐derived, animal‐origin, and microorganism‐generated sources. Then, this review presents strategies to improve the
performance of biomass‐derived carbon in supercapacitors, including heteroatom doping, surface functionalization, and hybrid
composite construction. Furthermore, this review analyzes the functions of biomass‐derived carbon in supercapacitors both in
its pure form and as modified materials. The review also explores composites derived from biomass‐based carbon, including
carbon/MXenes, carbon/MOFs, carbon/graphene, carbon/conductive polymers, carbon/transition metal oxides, and carbon/
hydroxides, providing a thorough investigation. Most importantly, this review offers an innovative summary and analysis of the
role of biomass‐derived carbon in supercapacitors through theoretical calculations, concentrating on four key aspects: energy
band structure, density of states, electron cloud density, and adsorption energy. Finally, the review concludes the future
research directions for biomass carbon‐based supercapacitors, including the discovery of novel biomass materials, tailoring
surface functional groups, fabricating high‐performance composite materials, exploring ion transfer mechanisms, and
enhancing practical applications. In summary, this review offers a thorough exploration of the sources, functions, and mech-
anisms of biomass‐derived carbon in supercapacitors, providing valuable insights for future research.

ABSTRACT
The synthesis of porous hard carbon from coconut biomass waste using physical activation through pyrolysis and 
chemical activation with orange juice as an organic activator at varying temperatures, including 500 
◦
C, 600 
◦
C, 
and 700 
◦
C, has been carried out. The purpose of this research is to develop materials for faradaic-type super -
capacitor electrodes based on these temperature variations. Characterization and testing methods used include X- 
ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET), cyclic voltammetry 
(CV), and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS). BET analysis showed that the PHC-700 sample 
exhibited a relatively high specific surface area with porous characteristics and a narrow pore size distribution 
around 17 – 18 nm. The PHC-700 sample also exhibited the best electrochemical performance with a specific 
capacitance of 485.23 F/g and a total resistance of 24.29 Ω . GCD measurements revealed stable triangular 
curves, indicating good charge-discharge reversibility and confirming the superior capacitive behavior of PHC- 
700. The study confirmed that the higher the temperature used, the better the supercapacitor electrode obtained. 
This is evidenced by the pores on the surface that help improve the quality of the electrode and the XRD test 
results which are directly proportional to the increase in temperature. It is hoped that this research can enhance 
understanding of supercapacitor electrode applications.
1. Introduction
The rapid development of the global economy and shifts in energy 
consumption patterns are posing a significant challenge to environ -
mental sustainability [ 1 ]. In an international context, the increasing 
energy demand is driven by rapid urbanization, industrialization, and 
the growing use of electronic devices in almost all aspects of human life. 
On the other hand, the supply of fossil fuels, the primary source of 
traditional energy, is dwindling and becoming increasingly limited. This 
not only impacts energy security but also contributes to accelerated 
global climate change, which is primarily caused by greenhouse gas 
emissions resulting from the burning of fossil fuels. In light of these 
concerns, the search for more environmentally friendly and sustainable 
solutions to meet the world ’ s energy needs has become increasingly 
urgent. One of the alternatives that has garnered significant attention is 
renewable energy, particularly solar and wind energy. These two energy 
sources are considered a promising solution because they are environ -
mentally friendly and do not produce carbon emissions, which is crucial 
in mitigating the impact of global climate change.
Solar energy, obtained through solar panels, and wind energy, ob -
tained through wind turbines, are abundant and renewable natural re -
sources. The main advantages of these energies are their unlimited 
availability and their ability to reduce dependence on fossil fuels. In 
addition, these two sources of energy play a crucial role in creating a 
more decentralized energy model, where each individual or community 
can produce and manage their energy. However, despite their great 
potential, the use of renewable energy such as solar and wind also comes 
with significant challenges. One of them is the dependence on external 
factors that are difficult to control, namely the weather. Solar energy can 
only be generated when the weather is clear, while wind energy can only

1. Introduction
The finite resources of fossil fuels, continuous population growth, 
and technological advancements pose energy shortage challenges for 
humanity [ 1 , 2 ]. Therefore, renewable energy development has become 
the current energy trend [ 3 , 4 ]. However, the regional limitations of 
renewable energy and the issue of power storage present significant 
challenges in their application [ 5 ]. Hence, until a breakthrough in power 
generation technology occurs, energy storage devices play a critical role 
[ 6 ]. Supercapacitors combine the rapid charging and discharging ca -
pabilities of capacitors with the high energy storage capacity of batte -
ries. This allows them to deliver quick energy bursts and store significant 
power, making them suitable for various applications, from consumer 
electronics to industrial equipment. Their capacity to endure frequent 
charge cycles without considerable degradation makes them highly 
efficient and reliable in demanding situations [ 7 , 8 ]. It integrates the fast 
charge and discharge capabilities found in capacitors with the robust 
energy storage capacity of batteries, offering a unique solution that 
harnesses both technologies ’ strengths to deliver both rapid energy 
bursts and long-term power storage [ 9 , 10 ]. Supercapacitors offer several 
benefits compared to traditional options, including higher power 
density, fast charge and discharge rates, extended lifespan, excellent 
cycle stability, and low sensitivity to temperature changes [ 11 ]. These 
advantages make their application range extremely wide, encompassing 
energy supply, vehicle transportation, mobile communications, artificial 
intelligence, biosensing, medical equipment, and wearable devices 
[ 12 – 14 ].
Biomass carbon, a carbon-rich material similar to charcoal, is pro -
duced by thermally decomposing biological waste (such as food and 
agricultural residues) in a limited oxygen environment [ 15 – 19 ]. Owing 
to its physicochemical properties, including a large surface area, sig -
nificant pore volume, and unique functional groups, it holds great 
promise as an exceptional alternative to activated carbon for use as an 
adsorbent [ 20 – 24 ]. The effectiveness of biomass carbon production is 
determined by various carbonization and activation factors, such as the 
type of biomass, temperature, duration, and choice of activating agent 
[ 21 , 25 ]. The largest quantities of biomass, which are abundant and 
renewable globally, typically come from agricultural waste, forest resi -
dues, wood processing by-products, and energy crops [ 26 , 27 ].
Coffee is the second largest agricultural product after tea, making 
coffee grounds a noteworthy subject of study in food waste [ 28 – 30 ].

ABSTRACT
Excessive fossil fuel use has caused severe pollution and global warming, making the adoption of clean, efficient, 
and renewable energy essential. This study focuses on synthesizing the Ni@MCTAC nanocomposite, comprising 
multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs), activated carbon from Conocarpus tree bark (AC-CTB), and Ni 
nanoparticles, using a straightforward ultrasonic technique. Structural and morphological analyses reveal Ni and 
MWCNTs attached to the AC-CTB surface in the Ni@MCTAC nanocomposite. The Ni@MCTAC nanocomposite 
(1034 m

. The fabricated ASC powered a blue LED for over 5 min, show -
casing its excellent performance. This highlights the potential of the Ni@MCTAC nanocomposite as a binder-free, 
flexible electrode for asymmetric supercapacitor.
1. Introduction
The increasing energy demand, and vastly depleting fossil fuels are 
the two main reasons to create the research interest towards clean, 
green, and renewable energy sources for energy production and storage. 
In the last few decades, fuel cells and batteries have played a major role 
in our earth's indispensable energy requirements but the two funda -
mental components of systems that continuously store and distribute 
energy are traditional capacitors and batteries. Batteries, on the other 
hand, provide a substantial amount of energy with low power density, 
whereas ordinary capacitors have no energy density but provide high 
power density [ 1 – 5 ]. As a result, attention to evolve the improved high- 
power, and high-energy density energy storage devices has been focused 
by many researchers [ 6 , 7 ].
Supercapacitors (SCs) are one kind of energy storage system that has 
captivated a lot of scientific interest today. Supercapacitors have two 
distinct methods of storing energy: electrical double-layer capacitance 
(EDLC) and pseudocapacitance. Carbonaceous materials with excess 
conductivity and high surface areas like activated carbon (AC), gra -
phene, and carbon nanotubes (CNTs) are known as EDLC electrode 
materials [ 8 , 9 ]. On the other side, metal oxides, carbides, nitrides, sel -
enides, and conducting polymers undergo reversible redox reactions 
which are pseudocapacitive electrode materials because of their abun -
dance in nature, cost-effectiveness, and extraordinary capacity to store

Abstract
Background: Porous carbon electrode (PCE) is identi ﬁed as a highly suitable electrode material for commercial application due
to its production process, which is characterized by simplicity, cost-effectiveness and environmental friendliness. PCE was syn-
thesized using torch ginger (Etlingera elatior (Jack) R.M. Smith) leaves as the base material. The leaves were treated with differ-
ent concentrations of ZnCl
2, resulting in a supercapacitor cell electrode with unique honeycomb-like three-dimensional
(3D) morphological pore structure. This PCE comprises nano ﬁbers from lignin content and volatile compounds from aromatic
biomass waste.
Results: From the characterization of physical properties, PCE-0.3 had an impressive amorphous porosity, wettability and 3D
honeycomb-like structural morphology with a pore framework consisting of micropores and mesopores. According to the struc-
tural advantages of 3D hierarchical pores such as interconnected honeycombs, PCE-0.3 as supercapacitor electrode had a high
speciﬁc capacitance of up to 285.89 F g −1 at 1 A. Furthermore, the supercapacitor exhibited high energy and power density of
21.54 Wh kg −1 and 161.13 W kg −1, respectively, with a low internal resistance of 0.059 Ω.
Conclusion: The results indicated that 3D porous carbon materials such as interconnected honeycombs derived from the aro-
matic biomass of torch ginger leaves have signi ﬁcant potential for the development of sustainable energy storage devices.

1. Introduction 
In today's world, the consumption of fossil energy for portable 
electronic devices, electronic vehicles, and other energy-consuming 
industrialization are increasing day by day and the demand of the en -
ergy causing environmental pollution and economic issues. [ 1 , 2 ]. With 
the increase in necessity for energy, it becomes necessary to store energy 
and use it efficiently. Advanced energy storage devices such as fuel 
batteries, supercapacitors and rechargeable batteries have been suc -
cessfully relieve environmental problems and energy shortage [ 3 , 4 ]. 
Among the advanced energy storage systems, Supercapacitors are the 
main energy storage system that has attracted more attention due to 
their long cycling stability, extremely low internal resistance, high 
power density capability, fast charge-discharge cycling, and longer life 
span [ 5 ]. The supercapacitor is mainly classified into three groups ac -
cording to the energy storage mechanism: Electrode double layer ca -
pacitors (EDLC), Pseudocapacitors, and Hybrid capacitors. In recent 
years, the combination of EDLC and pseudocapacitor in the hybrid 
capacitor has attracted attention due to its high performance, good 
cycling stability, and excellent specific capacitance [ 6 – 8 ]. 
The hybrid supercapacitor is largely dependent on the nature of 
Electrodes, electrolyte, separators and current collectors. The carbon 
based electrodes such as carbon nanotube (CNT), carbon nanofiber, 
graphene, activated carbon (AC), carbon aerogel, etc. are considered to 
be the ideal electrode materials in the supercapacitor because of their 
physiochemical properties such as high chemical stability, high specific 
surface area, excellent electrical conductivity, etc. [ 9 – 11 ]. In recent 
years, biomass-derived carbon materials synthesized from various

Batteries 2026, 12, 18  https://doi.org/10.3390/batteries12010018 
Review 
Recent Progress of Biomass‐Derived Carbon for  
Supercapacitors: A Review 
Anlin Li 1, Junming Xu 2,* and Jipeng Cheng 3,4,* 
1  Hangzhou Emust Technology Co., Ltd., Hangzhou 311300, China; lianlin@emust.com.cn 
2  College of Electronic Information, Hangzhou Dianzi University, Hangzhou 310018, China 
3  School of Materials Science and Engineering, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou 310058, China 
4  Longmen Laboratory of Luoyang, Luoyang 471000, China 
*  Correspondence: xujunming@hdu.edu.cn (J.X.); chengjp@zju.edu.cn (J.C.) 
Abstract 
Carbon materials are  very important for the commercial production of supercapacitors 
and they are crucial electrode materials. The porous carbon prepared with biomass ma-
terials as a  precursor is of signiﬁcance due to  its  sustainability, environmental friendli-
ness, and low cost. Biomass-derived carbon (BDC) has been widely investigated and re-
ported as the electrode of supercapacitors  due  to  its  abundant  pores  and  high  surface 
areas. In this work, the recent advancement of BDC for supercapacitors in the last three 
years  is  reviewed.  The  energy  storage  mechanism,  synthesis  techniques,  and  biomass 
classiﬁcation  of  BDC  are  brieﬂy  summarized  at  the  beginning  of  this  work.  Some  new 
typical  cases  with  diﬀerent  biomass  resources  as  raw  materials  are  addressed.  Then, 
eﬀective  strategies  to  further  improve  the  speciﬁc  capacitance  of  BDC,  including  het-
eroatoms  doping,  designing  composites,  novel  processes,  enhancing  graphitic  degree, 
and unique preparation methods, are discussed in detail. Finally, the challenges and fu-
ture perspectives of porous BDC for supercapacitors are outlined. 
Keywords: supercapacitors; biomass materials; porous carbon; energy storage 
 
1. Introduction 
With  the  rapid  growth  of  the  population  and  the  exploration  of  energy-intensive 
technologies, the consumption of energy is rapidly increasing in the world. The excessive 
usage of traditional energy sources including natural gas, coal, and fossil fuels results in 
serious  global  climate  changes  and  pollution.  Thus,  the  application  of  renewable  and 
clean energy, such as wind and solar power, is being driven by researchers and engineers 
[1]. Due to the intermittent nature of the renewables, novel devices to store energy with 
superior performance and excellent reliability are urgently needed to meet the growing 
energy  requirement,  including lithium and  sodium batteries,  aqueous  Zn-ion batteries, 
fuel cells, and supercapacitors [2]. These devices are expected to have not only large en-
ergy  densities  but  also  high  speciﬁc  power  [3].  Among  these  devices,  supercapacitors 
(SCs), also known  as electrochemical capacitors, have been intensively investigated be-
cause  of  their  many  advantages,  with  the  distinctive  features  of  fast  charging  and  dis-
charging rates, as well as long cycle life [4].

ABSTRACT  
The main aim of this research work is to make activated carbon (AC) materials based on biochar obtained from 
date seeds via pyrolysis and activated with H
2

4
. The study aimed to assess the potential of these biochar-based 
materials for energy storage in supercapacitor by investigating the impact of different activation temperatures on 
their electrochemical performance in an alkaline electrolyte. The focus was on identifying the most efficient 
material. Results from Raman Spectroscopy and XRD analysis revealed that sample DSAC-700 exhibited more 
ordered domains and suitable storage sites compared to the other biochar-based materials. Measured value of the 
ratio of intensity of D & G band (I

) for DSAC-700 indicated a higher ordered graphitic plane, 
resulting improved conductivity and diffusion of ions within the aligned graphitic domains, which positively 
impacted the electrochemical performance. Samples DSAC-700 showed 487.5 F/g specific capacitance at 1 A/g 
current density. Galvanic charge and discharge trends also showed that DSAC-700 had higher charge storage 
ability with less discharge. The biochar-based materials (BC and ACs) derived from DS showed promise as 
materials for energy storage applications, and they represent a step towards clean energy.   
1. Introduction 
Energy consumption worldwide has been steadily increasing, with 
levels reaching 575 quadrillion (BTU) in 2015 and projected to reach 
736 quadrillion BTU by 2040. But unfortunately, current energy re -
sources are insufficient to meet this demand and may result in signifi -
cant energy crises due to issues such as non-renewable nature of natural 
resources, environmental effects, and higher energy requirements [1,2] . 
It is imperative and pressing to prioritize the development of energy 
solutions that are efficient, inexpensive, simple to produce, and eco- 
friendly, including energy storage devices such as fuel cells, batteries, 
capacitors, and supercapacitors [3 – 6] . 
Amongst the energy storage devices, supercapacitors have several 
exceptional characteristics. These are fast charging and discharging, 
long and stable cycles, superior power and energy density that distin -
guish them from others. Due to these features, supercapacitors are seen 
as a complementary storage device to capacitors, fuel cells, and con -
ventional rechargeable batteries. The excellent performance of 
supercapacitors makes them useful in many applications, such as 
portable and consumer electronics, transportation, aerospace, and sen -
sors [7 – 9] . 
Based on energy storage mechanism, supercapacitors are categorized 
into two types which are electrical double layer capacitors (EDLCs) and 
pseudo-capacitors [10] . The performance of supercapacitors is highly 
influenced by the properties of the active electrode materials [11] . 
Carbon-nanotubes (CNTs), carbon-nanofibers (CNFs) and biomass 
derived graphene like carbon are some promising active materials for 
electrode that can be employed for electrical double layer capacitors 
(EDLCs). In contrast, pseudo-capacitive behavior mainly relies on 
carbon-based materials like metal oxides, metal hydroxides and con -
ducting polymers. Due to these material redox reactions occur during 
the charging and discharging processes [12 – 17] .

ABSTRACT  
Porous carbons possess considerable appeal and are in high demand as materials that can be produced from 
biomass waste. This study presents the transformation of Tectona grandis (Teak) sawdust into porous carbon 
materials, referred to as Tectona grandis sawdust-derived porous carbon (TPC), through a cost-effective FeCl
3
- 
assisted carbonization process, followed by a KOH activation. TPC samples were synthesized by carbonization at 
different temperatures (650 – 850 
◦
C) and characterized comprehensively. Structural analysis via X-Ray diffrac -
tion (XRD), Raman, and Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) revealed a progressive enhancement in 
graphitic structure and reduction of functional groups with increasing activation temperature. Field emission 
scanning electron microscopy (FESEM) displayed the development of intricate hollow tube-like porous networks 
in TPC-850, with the highest specific surface area (1767.66 m
2
/g) and pore volume (1.43 cm
3
/g). Electro -
chemical investigations showcased the superior performance of TPC-850 as a supercapacitor electrode due to its 
high graphitic nature, large surface area, and well-structured porosity. The galvanostatic charge-discharge (GCD) 
measurements exhibited a high specific capacitance of 572 F/g at 0.5 A/g in a 6 M KOH electrolyte. The high- 
frequency semicircle and low-frequency steeper region in electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) further 
indicated reduced resistance and enhanced ion diffusion in TPC-850. Significantly, TPC-850 demonstrated 
remarkable electrochemical cyclic stability, retaining 95.83 % of its initial capacity even after undergoing 4500 
cycles at a scan rate of 500 mV/s. The findings underscore the viability of TPC-850 as a high-performance 
supercapacitor electrode material, providing insights into harnessing renewable resources for advanced energy 
solutions. This work highlights the potential of utilizing waste biomass for energy storage applications and 
demonstrates the feasibility of converting it into efficient porous carbon materials with substantial graphitization 
and porosity.   
1. Introduction 
Over the last few decades, the depletion of fossil fuels, environmental 
contamination, and the release of greenhouse gases has led to significant 
health risks and disruptions in ecosystems. As a response, researchers 
are increasingly investigating environmentally friendly and sustainable 
systems for energy storage and conversion [ 1 – 4 ]. Renewable energy 
sources are being integrated into the energy sector, aiming to mitigate 
environmental pollution by reducing reliance on traditional, fossil fuel- 
based power methods [ 5 – 7 ]. Hence, there has been a growing fascina -
tion with nanomaterials due to their electrochemical characteristics, 
cost-effectiveness, simplicity in production, extensive surface area, and 
improved electrical as well as magnetic behaviour [ 8 , 9 ]. In particular, 
porous activated carbons derived from organic waste have emerged as a 
significant and innovative concept. This is primarily attributed to their 
widespread applications in eco-friendly electrochemical sensors, fuel 
cells, solar cells, catalysis, and energy storage devices such as batteries 
and supercapacitors [ 10 – 13 ]. Furthermore, these carbon materials are 
cost-effective, environmentally friendly, easily accessible, possess high 
carbon content, exhibit excellent electrical conductivity, and showcase 
remarkable physicochemical properties [ 4 ]. Specifically, the distinctive 
crystal structure found in carbon materials derived from biomass plays a 
crucial role in facilitating the swift movement of electrolyte ions within 
electrodes. This characteristic renders them highly promising materials 
for use as electrodes in supercapacitors [ 14 ].

Abstract: The present work reports the synthesis of biomass derived activated carbon and its elec-
trochemical behaviour in different electrolytes. Ricinus communis shell (RCS) was used as a raw
material in this study for the synthesis of activated carbon (AC) following a high-temperature acti-
vation procedure using potassium hydroxide as the activating agent. The physical and structural
characterization of the prepared Ricinus communis shell-derived activated carbon (RCS-AC) was
carried by Brunauer-Emmett-Teller analysis, X-ray diffraction analysis, Fourier Transform Infrared
Spectroscopy, Raman Spectroscopy and Scanning Electron Microscopy. The synthesized AC was elec-
trochemically characterized using various techniques such as Cyclic voltammetry (CV), galvanostatic
charge–discharge (GCD) tests, and Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) measurements in
different aqueous electrolytes (KOH, H2SO4, and Na2SO4). The results show that the double layer
properties of the RCS-AC material in different electrolytes are distinct. In speciﬁc, the working elec-
trode tested in 3 M KOH showed excellent electrochemical performance. It demonstrated a speciﬁc
capacitance of 137 F g−1 (at 1 A g−1 in 3 M KOH) and exhibited high energy and power densities of
18.2 W hkg−1 and 663.4 W kg−1, respectively. The observed capacitance in 3 M KOH remains stable
with 97.2% even after 5000 continuous charge and discharge cycles, indicating long-term stability.
The study conﬁrmed that the synthesized RCS-derived activated carbon (RCS-AC) exhibits good
stability and physicochemical characteristics, making them commercially promising and appropriate
for energy storage applications.

A huge amount of effort has been made in the recent years to develop renewable,
environmentally sustainable, affordable, and dependable energy systems. The gradual
deterioration of the atmosphere and the depletion of fossil resources have drawn the
attention of researchers and scientists towards the exploration of renewable energy [1–5].
There are two kinds of electrochemical devices: batteries and capacitors, both of which are
promising energy storage systems. Depending on the charge management mechanisms
used, all energy storage technologies have certain advantages and disadvantages. Batteries

high-power density but a low energy density [6–8]. A supercapacitor (SC), also known as
an electrochemical capacitor, is an intermediary between the battery and the traditional
capacitor that provides signiﬁcant advantages such as enhanced strength and energy ﬂow,
high reliability, ﬂexible operating temperature, and environmental friendliness [9,10]. The
